title: Token-priority health gating and soft-circuit policies to stabilize autoscaler handoffs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Production incidents in Jan/Feb showed autoscaler handoffs thrashing when a small percentage of high-token requests from a few enterprise customers caused readiness probes to fail and triggered aggressive scaling. This ticket implements a token-priority aware health gating layer plus a soft-circuit (degraded-mode) policy so we can preserve SLOs during regional capacity transitions without immediate hard failover.

Problem: Current readiness/liveness probes treat all requests equally and feed binary signals to the autoscaler. Large token requests inflate latency tails and intermittent probe failures cause the autoscaler to both scale up and evict capacity aggressively (thrash) during multi-region failover windows. This leads to temporary SLO breaches, customer errors, and excessive cost.

Proposed solution: 1) Add a lightweight token-priority classifier that annotates probes and synthetic transactions. 2) Implement adaptive readiness windows: probe health score is aggregated with exponential decay and token-weighted bucketing so heavy-token requests do not dominate. 3) Introduce a soft-circuit policy: when aggregated health drops below a conservative threshold, mark region as DEGRADED (soft-breaker) and trigger controlled shedding of low-priority traffic, extend autoscaler cooldowns, and avoid hard failover unless regional capacity remains low after a grace period. 4) Add synthetic warmup transactions targeted at cold pods to help the autoscaler make more informed decisions. 5) Expose control knobs in Console for per-customer token-priority overrides and an emergency bypass.

Why unique: This is not just another probe smoothing change — we combine request-shape awareness (token counts), priority-weighted shedding, and autoscaler damping into a unified policy that preserves high-priority customers while preventing global cascading scale events.
acceptance_criteria: Health score includes token-weighted buckets and p50/p95/p99 breakdowns in metrics
When region enters DEGRADED soft-breaker: low-priority requests are shed per policy and high-priority customers continue to be served within SLO targets
Autoscaler cooldowns extend by configured factor during DEGRADED state and do not immediately trigger hard failover
Synthetic warmups reduce cold-start latency by >=30% for affected pods in staging
E2E canary demonstrates no SLO breach for high-priority synthetic traffic during injected load test (see chaos test)
implementation_notes: Runtime: add request token histogram tagging and expose token-priority header for internal use
Proxy: add a lightweight admissions filter that increments token-shaped counters used by health aggregation
Controller: new soft-circuit state machine (OK -> WARN -> DEGRADED -> RECOVERING) with configurable hysteresis and cooldown damping
Autoscaler: add 'degraded_cooldown_multiplier' that multiplies default cooldown during DEGRADED state
Metrics: new metric 'health_score.token_weighted' and dashboard panels for per-tenant token distribution
Feature flag: token_priority_health_gating rollout flag with per-region and per-tenant scope
rollout_plan: Phase 1: feature flag off (tests + staging) -> Phase 2: enable token-priority metrics and synthetic warmups in staging -> Phase 3: enable soft-breaker in a single canary region for low-traffic orgs -> Phase 4: expand to high-traffic tenants with customer opt-in and monitoring gates. Rollback: disable flag and trigger immediate recovery state. Target full rollout by runtime-1.22 stable.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for health aggregation and state transitions. 2) Integration tests with autoscaler simulator (local). 3) Chaos test: inject bursty high-token traffic mixing low/high priority tenants and validate autoscaler no-thrash property. 4) Staging soak for 72h with synthetic tenants. 5) Post-rollout verification dashboard checks for 24h.
risks: Incorrect token-priority classification could preferentially allow noisy tenants — mitigation: safe default to equal-weight until customer mappings validated
Adding soft-breaker state increases system complexity for operators — mitigation: observability + runbook + gradual rollout
Feature flag misconfiguration may leave regions in DEGRADED unexpectedly — mitigation: fail-safe that auto-recovers after max_grace_period
